title: Microsoft Teams: customise the recording and transcription notification and consent text
summary: The briefing passes: its controls, licensing statements and rollout facts are supported, and it clearly reports the conflicting PowerShell release warning. Minor corrections should finish the upload path and identify the source for the later calls roadmap item.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes IT admins customising the message and privacy link for implicit notification or explicit consent to recording and transcription.
claims.quote: IT admins can customize the message and privacy link used to notify implicitly or gain explicit consent from meeting participants for the use of recording, transcription during the meeting.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The custom notification toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Show customized in-meeting notification for recording and transcription.
claims.quote: Navigate to Meetings → Meeting policies. Select or create a meeting policy where you want to enable custom messages. In the Recording & transcription section, find the new setting: Show customized in-meeting notification for recording and transcription.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EnableRecordingAndTranscriptionCustomMessage $true is the documented custom notification toggle command, subject to the briefing's PowerShell release warning.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect. This policy controls whether custom strings can be shown for recording and transcription in user's Teams meetings. It need to work with RecordingAndTranscriptionCustomMessageIdentifier.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Customize notification reaches the panel for custom message text.
claims.quote: Click the Customize notification button to set your custom message. Download the CSV template from the customization panel. [...] Upload the completed CSV using the Select a file button.
claims.fix: Finish controls[1].ui.path at the upload control: 'Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Customize notification > Select a file', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/recording-transcription-custom-message.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -RecordingAndTranscriptionCustomMessageIdentifier <Guid> assigns the custom message identifier, subject to the stated release warning.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect. This attribute holds the unique identifier for the custom recording and transcription meeting message. It stores a GUID that points to the CustomMessage in TeamsCustomMessageConfiguration.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; rendered controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The privacy URL control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting settings > Email invitation > Privacy and security URL.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, expand Meetings > Meeting settings. Under Email invitation, do the following: [...] Privacy and security URL If your organization has a legal website that you want people to go to for any legal concerns, enter the URL here.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -LegalURL <String> sets the tenant privacy URL also used in meeting invitations.
claims.quote: -LegalURL [...] URL to a website containing legal information and meeting disclaimers. This would be included in the meeting invite. Please ensure this URL is publicly accessible for invites that go beyond your federation boundaries

claims.claim: The explicit consent toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting Policies > policy > Recording & Transcription > Require participant agreement for recording and transcription.
claims.quote: Under Meetings, select Meeting Policies. [...] Within your chosen policy, navigate to the Recording & Transcription section. Toggle the Require participant agreement for recording and transcription setting On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent Enabled requires participant agreement for recording and transcription.
claims.quote: To require participants to give their explicit consent to be recorded or transcribed in any meeting that organizers with this policy create, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent Enabled

claims.claim: Off (Disabled) is the default for the explicit participant agreement setting.
claims.quote: Off | Disabled | This setting is the default value. For organizers with this policy, participants aren't asked for consent to be recorded and transcribed.

claims.claim: Turning on explicit consent causes the explicit consent scenario notifications to be used.
claims.quote: Turn on explicit consent: With this on, users see the "explicit consent scenario" notifications.

claims.claim: If no privacy and security URL is entered, Teams displays the Microsoft Entra ID privacy policy.
claims.quote: If you don't enter a privacy and security URL in Teams meeting settings or PowerShell, we display Microsoft Entra ID's privacy policy. [...] If there's no Microsoft Entra ID, we display the Microsoft Privacy policy.

claims.claim: External tenant users instead see the Microsoft Privacy policy when no custom privacy URL is configured.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Entra ID's privacy policy isn't shown to external tenant users or anonymous users. If you don't create a privacy and security URL in Teams meeting settings or PowerShell, the Microsoft Privacy policy is shown instead.

claims.claim: Anonymous users instead see the Microsoft Privacy policy when no custom privacy URL is configured.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Entra ID's privacy policy isn't shown to external tenant users or anonymous users. If you don't create a privacy and security URL in Teams meeting settings or PowerShell, the Microsoft Privacy policy is shown instead.

claims.claim: Using <empty> for a language or scenario leaves only fixed notification information.
claims.quote: If you don't want to display any message (excluding the fixed information), you can insert `<empty>` for the specific language or scenario. In this case, the notification shows only the fixed information.

claims.claim: Learn warns that Excel uses different CSV delimiters in some non-English system languages.
claims.quote: In some non-English system languages (for example, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and other European locales), Excel uses a different default CSV delimiter based on regional settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft tells admins using those languages to use a plain text editor rather than edit or re-save the template in Excel.
claims.quote: To avoid formatting issues, admins using these system languages should edit the CSV template using another plain text editor. Please do not edit or re-save the CSV file using Excel.

claims.claim: New-CsTeamsRecordingAndTranscriptionCustomMessage creates the message set whose generated identifier is assigned for custom messages.
claims.quote: After this configuration is successfully completed, you can assign the generated Id to the user's RecordingAndTranscriptionCustomMessageIdentifier field to apply the policy to that user.
